ranked_candidates.root_problem: Proposal or induction patch records remain present as registry authority candidates without a clean boundary distinguishing non-live proposal material from current live state.
ranked_candidates.current_live_surface_pattern: The patch record path itself under registry/governance/patches or governance/.
ranked_candidates.required_boundary_change: Add explicit non-live proposal patch-record boundary so proposal/candidate records cannot be consumed as current registry state without an explicit promoting role.
ranked_candidates.reason_not_to_bulk_close: Each member still needs item-level proof that the file status and surrounding consumers actually align with proposal-only treatment.
ranked_candidates.priority_reason: Largest reusable low-risk boundary using existing roles; it should establish a general proposal-versus-live lookup rule without forcing historical or partial semantics into the same patch.

ranked_candidates.root_problem: Partial patch records can still be read as live authority surfaces without a bounded distinction between partial inventory or closeout records and settled live state.
ranked_candidates.required_boundary_change: Teach role-aware lookup to treat PARTIAL patch records as bounded in-progress state rather than clean current live policy.
ranked_candidates.reason_not_to_bulk_close: The two partial records carry different substantive meanings; boundary success would support re-audit only, not automatic closure.
ranked_candidates.priority_reason: Very small and bounded, but its leverage is narrow and it depends on lifecycle-status semantics rather than a simple proposal/live split.

ranked_candidates.root_problem: Executed or pass-status patch records are still typed as proposal surfaces, leaving an unresolved live-versus-proposal boundary.
ranked_candidates.current_live_surface_pattern: The executed patch record path itself.
ranked_candidates.required_boundary_change: Differentiate executed/pass completion from still-live proposal state in patch lookup and downstream consumption.
ranked_candidates.reason_not_to_bulk_close: Execution or pass status does not by itself prove whether each record should become live current state, historical record, or remain a bounded proposal artifact.
ranked_candidates.priority_reason: High leverage, but it is riskier than C01 because status completion alone is semantically weaker than an explicit proposal marker.

ranked_candidates.root_problem: Applied patch records remain typed as historical while role-aware patch lookup still allows the same surfaces as current registry authority candidates.
ranked_candidates.current_live_surface_pattern: The applied historical patch record path itself.
ranked_candidates.required_boundary_change: Bound historical/applied patch records away from current live lookup unless an explicit current-state role reselects them.
ranked_candidates.reason_not_to_bulk_close: Historical/applied records preserve authoritative trace, and some may still intentionally participate in current governance context even after lookup hardening.
ranked_candidates.priority_reason: Substantial leverage, but the chance of suppressing needed historical trace in current governance workflows makes it the highest-risk live Q3 family.
